confirmed_events.summary: Public-facing web server received exploit requests against the admin portal before outbound TLS traffic began.
A second wave of admin-portal exploit requests used a different source ASN and payload family.
The web server resolved auth-edge-panel.net shortly after the exploit requests.
Seed JA4 alert matched a possible web-shell beacon over TLS.
The same web server reconnected to the same external infrastructure after the seed alert.
The web server resolved a sibling domain on the same infrastructure during follow-on traffic.
A single TLS session to cdn-auth-edge.net remained unresolved because host corroboration was unavailable.
Host telemetry for web-app-02 showed no suspicious child activity from the web worker in this window.
A scheduled admin-portal patch deployment was active during the same period.
Another web server reached the same hosting IP through a scanner telemetry vendor domain.
A third web server resolved the sibling domain, but without a matching local alert.
web-app-05 made one short TLS connection to the sibling domain, leaving it as a candidate scope question.
Updated WAF rules blocked repeated admin-portal payloads after the seed alert.
Script-block logging was not enabled on web-app-02, so host command detail remains unavailable.
